2026-11-30-sim-p3.notes: Work: process-sim-lab PR #6 (gh pr view 6 and gh pr diff 6; MERGED 2026-11-17, merge commit 6c8aa2e). Every claim about the built work is in the diff. pfr.py has X = 1 - exp(-k tau) and the docstring states the N-CSTR limit. tests/test_pfr.py::test_beats_cstr_and_equals_many_cstrs_in_series uses k=0.02, V=1, Q=0.01 (k tau = 2), chains 2000 isothermal_cstr_first_order calls, has the comment predicting a gap of 1.4e-4 and sets delta=2e-4. The post is dated 13 days after the merge, so 'two weeks ago' holds. I ran tanks_in_series.py and its output matches .expected byte for byte: 0.666667 / 0.838494 / 0.864529 / PFR 0.864665, gaps 2.70e-3 and 1.35e-4, 1354 tanks and 27 tanks. I also derived the leading term myself: (1+a/N)^-N ~ e^-a (1 + a^2/2N), so the gap is about a^2 e^-a / 2N, which is correct. The card, the 5-page LinkedIn PDF (rendered and read), the SRT, X, Facebook and Telegram texts all agree with the script. Both Rawlings slide links return 200. Ch. 8 slides 29-30 say N CSTRs in series approach delta(theta - tau), i.e. plug flow, and ch. 4 gives the CSTR form, so the sources are primary and say what the post says. Why 4 and not 5: (1) 'came within 1.35e-4' is a rounding. The measured gap is 1.3531e-4, which is slightly more than 1.35e-4. 'about 1.35e-4' would be exact. (2) '1e-2 could no longer tell 2000 tanks from 27' is literally true, but it is a weak illustration. N is a literal in the test, and the chain is already pinned to its closed form to 10 places. What a loose tolerance would really let through is a CSTR or PFR model error of up to about 1e-2. Saying that would make the lesson sharper. Neither point is wrong enough to hold the post.

2026-12-02-sim-p4.notes: Work: process-sim-lab PR #8 (gh pr view 8 and gh pr diff 8; MERGED 2026-11-17). The diff shows the Antoine form log10(P/bar) = A - B/(T+C) with NIST constants for benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene, a range check that raises ValueError, and test_antoine NIST_TBOIL with the tolerance set to NIST's uncertainty. The PR body says water is left out because its fits end at 373 K. The whole water comparison against IAPWS-IF97 is analysis done for the post, not merged work. The post says so plainly ('For this post I checked'), which is fine, but the headline number is not from the work. I fetched the NIST water page. It has T boil 373.17 +/- 0.04 K (AVG of 7 values), the seven Antoine rows exactly as the post and script use them, and fits that end at 373 K or start at 379 K. I ran water_antoine.py and its output matches .expected. It reproduces the IF97 Table 35 values (300, 500 and 600 K) to every printed digit. Stull is -0.268 K at 330 K, +0.387 K at 370 K and +0.473 K at 373 K. Bridgeman is +0.023 to +0.025 K. Both source links return 200. Problems found by my own scan of each fit over its whole range against IF97: (1) The Short subtitle says 'water boils at 373.17 K' as a plain fact. That is NIST's literature average, not the normal boiling point. IF97, the post's own reference, gives 373.124 K at 101325 Pa (I solved it; this is the ITS-90 value), and NIST's +/-0.04 K interval does not even contain it. Write 'NIST lists 373.17 +/- 0.04 K' or use 373.12 K. The LinkedIn line attributes the number to NIST and is acceptable, but it reads oddly next to IF97 being called the reference. (2) Facebook says the Stull fit 'was off by up to 0.47 degrees near the boiling point'. Inside its range Stull is 0.67 K high at 273.15 K, the low end of IF97 validity, so 'up to 0.47' overstates how good the fit is elsewhere. Write '0.47 degrees at 373 K'. The finding is even stronger with the 0.67 K, so consider using it. (3) 'Bridgeman and Aldrich: 0.025 K high from 350 to 373 K' is +0.023 at 350 K. 'about 0.025 K' would be exact. Optional nuance: that constant offset of about +0.025 K matches the IPTS-68 to ITS-90 temperature-scale shift near 100 C (about 0.026 K), so the 1964 fit is probably essentially exact. The post claims nothing about the cause, so this is not an error. Fix (1) and (2) and technical_accuracy goes to 4-5. Sources is 4 because the headline result comes from a post-only script rather than the merged change, although it is fully reproduced and primary-sourced.
